# Scene RSI pilot smoke: historical evidence synthesis

## Scope and evidence matrix

The group contains two supplied student trajectories, not two copies of one trial. Both concern single-image Blender reconstruction. The audit reports cover all explicit model-reviewed chunks for both files; the underlying image pixels are not visible in the supplied observations. Citations identify the original JSONL files and their reported lines.

| Source and original path | Attempt and observed outcome | Feedback, update and validation |
|---|---|---|
| **S0200** — `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/smoke/smoke_01/trajectory.jsonl` | A 256 × 171 indoor-image reconstruction. Step 1 failed on a sink-rim fillet; step 2 failed on a missing Blender world; step 3 reported success, saved a render and scene, and was selected (lines 1, 5, 10, 15–16). | Tracebacks were received and followed by code revisions (lines 6, 8–9, 11, 13–14). The reference and render were then supplied with no executions remaining; the student answered `DONE`, without a visible written comparison or correction (lines 17–19). Technical execution succeeded; visual fidelity remains unknown. |
| **S0201** — `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/smoke/smoke_02/trajectory.jsonl` | A 170 × 256 indoor-image reconstruction. Step 1 failed on a chair-arm fillet; step 2 failed on a missing world; step 3 timed out after approximately 526 seconds, with no image and empty stdout/stderr (lines 1, 5, 10, 15). | The student received the tracebacks and executed revisions, including a reduced fillet and conditional world creation (lines 6, 8–9, 11, 13–14). The second execution passed the first failure; the final timeout leaves the world fix and overall build unverified. No visual comparison or formal success is recorded. |

## Comparison and interpretation

Both students programmed multi-object scenes from their own interpretations of the unseen references: a kitchen in S0200 and a reading corner in S0201. Those descriptions, the specified materials and poses, and intended connections between parts are **modeling intentions**, not independent observations of the photographs or finished geometry (S0200 lines 3–4; S0201 lines 3–4).

The common operational pattern was traceback-driven revision. Each first failure exposed a fillet radius incompatible with the affected part’s dimensions. S0200 changed the sink-rim construction; S0201 reduced the chair-arm radius. Each next execution reached a missing-world failure, after which the student added world creation (S0200 lines 5–14; S0201 lines 5–14). These observations support a transferable constraint: resolving one construction error can expose a separate environment assumption, and passing an earlier failure does not establish a complete working or visually accurate scene.

The outcomes nevertheless diverged. S0200’s third execution reported a saved render and scene, a technical success after two failures. The log reported 16 render samples although the program specified 48; neither the discrepancy’s cause nor its visual effect is established (lines 15–16). S0201’s third execution was interrupted by timeout, not shown to have failed for a diagnosed algorithmic reason. Its cause, including whether scene complexity contributed, is unknown (line 15). The S0201 student also changed camera, lighting and surface details before that execution, without a rendered view in evidence (lines 11, 13–14); the results of those aesthetic changes are unknown.

## Advice, acceptance and quality

No teacher detection, diagnosis, advice, receipt or adoption is recorded in either trajectory. The inputs that prompted the observed fixes were runner tracebacks, explicitly received in subsequent student requests, rather than teacher feedback. The resulting code changes were executed; their downstream validation differs as described above. S0200’s selected render and `DONE` establish neither a written visual diagnosis nor independent acceptance of scene quality. S0201 has no recorded rendered image to compare. Missing formal scores are unknown, and old model cost cannot be recovered from their absence.

The specific rim reconstruction, chair-arm radius and Blender world handling are task-specific facts, not proven general remedies. Whether either scene matched its reference in object placement, geometry, materials, camera, lighting or occlusion remains unverified. S0200 is a counterexample to treating every run as interrupted; S0201 is a counterexample to treating traceback-driven revisions as sufficient for completion. Neither record shows an empty patch, a permission, branch or CLI stop, or a teacher-led update; their absence here does not establish their absence elsewhere.

## Coverage statement

This is batch 1 of 1 for `scene_rsi_pilot__smoke`: both listed files, S0200 and S0201, are represented. The supplied reports state full observation of their respective 19 and 15 JSONL units. Conclusions are limited to the reported trajectory events and do not extend to unseen image pixels or independent quality assessment. This synthesis is audit-only.
